output.name: Óllun
output.myth: Óllun was a sailor who asked the wind where it stopped. He took his boat south past the last kelp, until the water went smooth and the stars came up strange. Aun had gone that way and not come back, and Óllun thought he might find him. Tavo the Gale laughed at the bow beside Tanhá, the Gale's Tooth, and would not push him on. Thavesk, the Turned Wake, tilted the water under him. Óllun reached the edge of the Unflown, looked over, and turned his boat around. Ommen the Lamp Boat, to the north, had lanterns for the drowned, and that was the light he steered for. He had not found the end of the wind, only the place where it stopped being kind. Hesk, who keeps count, wrote his name on the reel and said nothing. His lantern still hangs on the mast, pointing home. His hull faces the wrong way, south, where lost things go. Sil looks every month and never finds the boat. My grandmother says if you fly a kite on a still night and feel nothing pull, that is Óllun turning around.
output.finding: Sailors far to the south should find Tanhá, the Gale's Tooth, and Óllun lies about two-thirds of a hand-span straight north of it.
